title: Enzymes — Structure, Classification and Functions
shortDescription: Biological catalysts: how they work, how they are classified and why food technologists use them.
genZNote: Enzymes are the cheat codes of biology — same reaction, millions of times faster. Know the six EC classes and you're ahead of the meta.

sections.heading: Structure and Mechanism
bullets: Enzymes are mostly globular proteins (some RNA) that lower activation energy; the active site binds substrate (lock-and-key, induced-fit models).
Cofactors: metal ions; coenzymes (NAD+, FAD, CoA — derived from vitamins); holoenzyme = apoenzyme + cofactor.
Michaelis–Menten kinetics: Vmax and Km (substrate concentration at half Vmax; low Km = high affinity).
Factors: temperature (optimum ~37 °C in animals; denature above), pH (pepsin ~2, trypsin ~8), substrate/enzyme concentration, inhibitors (competitive, non-competitive).

sections.heading: Enzymes in Food Technology
bullets: Rennet/chymosin: cheese; lactase: lactose-free milk; α-amylase and glucoamylase: glucose syrups; invertase: confectionery; pectinase: juice clarification; papain/bromelain: meat tenderisation; catalase/peroxidase blanching indicators.
Blanching (steam/hot water) inactivates peroxidase/catalase to stop enzymatic deterioration during frozen storage.
Immobilised enzymes (adsorption, entrapment, covalent binding) allow reuse.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Enzymes are biological catalysts, usually proteins, that accelerate specific reactions and are widely exploited in food processing and analysis.
keyFacts: Km: substrate concentration at ½ Vmax.

highYieldFacts: Glucose isomerase converts glucose to fructose (HFCS).
commonTraps: Enzymes are not consumed in the reaction.
mustRemember: Hydrolases = largest group in food use.

questions.prompt: Glucose isomerase is used to produce:
questions.explanation: HFCS is made by isomerising glucose to fructose.
